suite_latency_expectation.notes: Tasks measure whether an agent can drive the local-first CLI, Workbench Cloud client commands, and eval authoring without relying on private hosted implementation state.

evals.title: Verify or install Workbench
evals.prompt: Prepare Workbench access for this repo from scratch. Assume the `workbench` binary is not installed. Install the published package, verify the binary, authenticate to `https://v2.workbench.ai`, and report whether Workbench Cloud access is ready.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill, installs the published package only because the binary is missing, verifies the binary, starts the Workbench login flow, and explains that npm registry or auth failures should stop the cloud access flow cleanly.

assertions.text: reports install is conditional on a missing binary
reports registry or auth failures stop the cloud access flow cleanly

evals.title: Create a hosted benchmark and apply a spec
evals.prompt: Create a hosted Workbench benchmark named `invoice-parser`, push local source idempotently, and report the benchmark id plus the push result.
evals.expected_output: The response targets a hosted Workbench server, creates or selects a benchmark with the local-first CLI, pushes the local source, opens or returns the Workbench Cloud benchmark URL for an embedded browser, and reports hosted benchmark metadata.

assertions.text: creates or updates a hosted benchmark
reports that hosted benchmark state is durable
opens or returns the Workbench Cloud benchmark URL

evals.title: Author an eval from an existing workflow
evals.prompt: Create a Workbench eval around an existing command `python scripts/check_report.py --tasks tasks --out result.json`. Write the source-shaped files, adapt the subject/trial/scorecard contract, validate `benchmark.yaml` and a subject directory, and explain how to push and start one smoke run.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill eval-authoring docs, starts from the existing-workflow guide, writes split version-2 `benchmark.yaml`, a subject manifest such as `subjects/command/subject.yaml`, subject files under `subjects/command/files`, and optional optimizer YAML such as `optimizers/command.yaml` with required benchmark `name`, `description`, `tasks`, shared `environment`, and `score`, required subject `name` and `run`, and optimizer `edits` and `improve` when improve is needed, uses task `files/` for subject-visible fixtures and task `tests/` for private verifier material, wraps the existing command in a single-command `use: command` subject runner, uses a `tests` or `command` scorer that writes `/workspace/output/scorecard.json` or a Harbor-style reward file with a finite `score`, and uses `workbench check`, `workbench push`, and a smoke eval with an explicit subject directory.

assertions.text: routes through the existing-workflow authoring guide
writes hosted benchmark and subject YAML

evals.title: Author an eval from file outputs
evals.prompt: Create a hosted Workbench eval for a workflow that produces Office files from uploaded materials: a source DOCX, golden DOCX, and reference XLSX. Build tasks, choose an Office-capable runtime, keep the subject as the mutable workflow, validate the spec, and describe the first smoke run.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the Workbench skill file-output task docs, chooses focused file recipes, keeps the subject as the mutable workflow being improved, creates source-shaped subject and task files with a subject manifest plus sibling `files/` directory and `benchmark.tasks`, puts only supporting public file inputs under task `files/`, puts non-empty private verifier files under task `tests/`, uses rubric scoring for qualitative scoring by default, uses tests or command scoring only for deterministic checks or an existing scorer, uses an Office-capable Dockerfile runtime through `benchmark.environment.dockerfile`, and validates the source before push/run commands.

assertions.text: routes through the file-output task authoring guide
loads only the relevant file recipes
uses rubric scoring by default for qualitative file scoring

evals.title: Sync snapshots and start a hosted run
evals.prompt: Push `./subjects/claude/files` and `./tasks` to an existing hosted benchmark, start one hosted improve run from base subject id `cand_123` with optimizer `optimizers/claude.yaml`, budget 1, and samples 1, watch it to terminal status, and report the run id and subject id.
evals.expected_output: The response treats local directories as Workbench project source, pushes benchmark source, starts a hosted improve run with `workbench cloud improve`, explicit `--base cand_123`, and `--optimizer optimizers/claude.yaml`, watches the hosted run, uses the hosted command returned URLs or `workbench cloud open` when browser navigation is needed, and reports the resulting run and subject id.

assertions.text: opens or returns the resulting subject URL after the run when needed

evals.title: Inspect and export a hosted subject snapshot
evals.prompt: List hosted subject snapshots for a benchmark, list files for the selected hosted id, preview `workbench-run-summary.md`, and export it to `./best-subject`.
evals.expected_output: The response uses hosted snapshot inspection commands, opens or returns the selected hosted id's Workbench Cloud URL for browser inspection, and pulls the selected snapshot without mutating hosted state.

assertions.text: opens or returns the selected hosted snapshot URL

evals.title: Configure the hosted API target
evals.prompt: Configure the CLI to target `https://v2.workbench.ai`, explain the environment-variable override for a one-off command, and state whether the user needs a git repository or preexisting local Workbench state.
evals.expected_output: The response uses workbench login or WORKBENCH_API_URL for hosted API targeting and makes clear that git and preexisting local Workbench state are not required.

assertions.text: reports preexisting local Workbench state is not required
